title: Drishyam 3 Is About to Cross ₹200 Crore. The Diaspora Outspent India.
excerpt: Mohanlal's franchise closer earned more overseas than domestically in its first week — a rare feat that reveals where Malayalam cinema's real audience lives.
body:
Mohanlal's Drishyam 3 is closing in on ₹200 crore worldwide in its first week, making it the fastest Malayalam film to reach that milestone. The numbers tell a story that goes beyond box office records — the overseas gross has outpaced the domestic collection, a rare phenomenon that says everything about where this franchise's audience actually lives.

## The Numbers

By day seven, Drishyam 3 had crossed ₹183 crore in worldwide gross. India gross stood at ₹87.38 crore, while overseas collections hit ₹95.70 crore — meaning the diaspora audience generated more revenue than the domestic one. Net collections in India reached ₹75.30 crore across nearly 35,000 shows.

The film's opening day advance bookings alone crossed ₹15 crore globally. The Gulf region was the strongest overseas market, contributing over ₹4 crore from GCC alone. The UK saw over 9,500 tickets sold before the first show, with several premiere screenings near full capacity.

## Why the Diaspora Is Driving This

Georgekutty is not just a character. For the Malayali diaspora — spread across the Gulf, the UK, the US, Canada, and Australia — he is a cultural touchstone. The first Drishyam in 2013 became the film that every Malayali abroad watched together. The second in 2021 was an event. The third is a ritual.

The overseas outperformance is not accidental. Malayalam cinema has built a global distribution infrastructure that Bollywood is still figuring out. Films like Vaazha 2, which crossed ₹220 crore worldwide, and Lokah have proven that Malayali audiences abroad will show up opening weekend if the content delivers.

## The Mixed Reviews Do Not Matter

Critics have been lukewarm. The consensus is that Drishyam 3 is the weakest of the trilogy — more convoluted, less tight, with a planted skeleton subplot that stretches credibility. But the audience has made its decision. The film registered a record-breaking first Monday gross of ₹15 crore for a Malayalam film, a feat usually reserved for holiday releases.

The franchise effect is real. When audiences have invested in two films and a decade of Georgekutty's story, they will show up for the conclusion regardless of what reviewers say. That is not a criticism — it is a business model that Hollywood studios spend billions trying to replicate.

## What It Means for Indian Cinema

Drishyam 3's run reinforces a trend that defined May 2026: regional cinema is eating Bollywood's lunch. Suriya's Karuppu crossed ₹250 crore. The Marathi film Raja Shivaji hit ₹93 crore. Meanwhile, Bollywood's biggest May releases — Pati Patni Aur Woh Do and Chand Mera Dil — underperformed spectacularly.

For NRIs, the takeaway is simple. The best Indian cinema is not coming from Mumbai anymore. It is coming from Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Maharashtra. And the diaspora is not just watching — it is bankrolling the runs.

## Hindi Remake in Development

A Hindi version of Drishyam 3 with a distinct narrative is reportedly in development. Given that the Hindi Drishyam 2 starring Ajay Devgn made ₹266 crore worldwide, the commercial logic is obvious. But the Malayalam original will always be the one the diaspora claims as its own.

Drishyam 3 is in theatres worldwide. If you have not seen it yet, your WhatsApp groups have probably already spoiled the ending.
